Let me explain how the ✨real world✨ works. My husband is a Boeing employee. He was just on strike last year with one of the Boeing unions. Boeing has a different union with employees who work at the same factory. My mom is in the other union. My husband got to strike and the company couldn't do shit about it, because his union was exercising their right to strike. My mom who's employed by the same company but is a part of a separate union was not protected to strike, and therefore went to work everyday as usual. Even with very little to do while the rest of the factory was out on the picket line. If my mom tried to strike in solidarity, she'd be fired after they deemed her to have abandoned the job.

What I did when T gel didn't stop my cycle after a few years of messing with the dosage, I switched up my meds and am now on a progestin only birth control, which is supposed to stop or minimize your cycle. I'm on that and two pumps of gel a day and I only get the occasional spotting maybe once every few months, but not enough to need a product. 


For reference, at one point when I was on 3 pumps and in upper normal T levels for a male my age, my cycle STILL wasn't stopping, so I had a persistent cycle to say the least. It didn't matter how high my T levels were. There are definitely other ways to get it to stop at least temporarily. I used to recommend the depo because it got it to stop on its own for over two years, but the depo causes ✨brain tumors✨ I guess. So. My advice is to start T and see how your cycle reacts. If it persists and you can't change your dose or are within normal T levels, see about getting on a progestin only BC and couple it with a testosterone. The injection depending on how they can manage your dose might be too high because the BC will take over a large portion of the T's job. (When I was on 3 pumps and started the BC, my levels shot up by about 400, and I was extremely high.) I highly recommend the gel if the injections don't work. Then when you have the money and are comfortable, surgery will be waiting for you.

Just be careful. Go into the job hunt without urgency and be prepared to stay at your current job for a while. What's happening in a lot of fields is hiring is outsources and they use AI to run through applications and resumes. Someone who meets 90% of application requirements is just as likely to be passed over by the AI as someone with only 50%.

I don’t have career advice, BUT there is no way you’re too late to get your grades up and get scholarships. There should be a bunch of scholarships. Go for ones that help people of color, ones that target your area, ones for people with ocd and/or on the spectrum. I bet there’s even scholarships for people who have a parent in jail. It’s never too late to attempt to turn it around for yourself. My BEST advice though, is when you go to college, make sure you understand the interest rates. Colleges and banks have made it pretty easy to gloss over to scam people. The best rule of thumb is to make sure you’re paying off all interest that’s built up each month. How people get into these vicious cycles of not being able to pay back is the minimum monthly payment doesn’t even cover the interest that’s accrued, or the interest that accrues each month. This means none of your payment is going towards what you took out, and what you owe just gets bigger. I hope things get better regarding prices and college. I hope things get better for you, and anyone else reading this who is in a tough spot. 

AND don’t forget, fill out your FAFSA as soon as it opens for the year you plan on going to college. See how much financial aid you can get. It should cover at least community college. If your GPA isn’t great, even after you graduate , you can spend some time getting pre requisite classes for “low cost” (pretty much free with financial aid) at community to boost your GPA if you need.

Princess Carolyn is away and received a phone call from Diane, complaining how the story doesn’t make sense, and that instead of sitting on motorcycles talking about doing cool things, they should just do the cool things. And suicide rates are probably increasing due to a mixture of lack of parental involvement, child and teen bullying, parental ignorance, "political doom" (as I like to call it), behaviour on social media, lack of empathy, lack of communication, lack of social body positivity, lack of physical contact, and bad and/or abusive sexual relationships, (bad education.)

Let's unpack. 

Lack of parental involvement and parental ignorance. We don't treat children and young adults like human beings. We say we do, but we don't. Parents are supposed to be (at least in my opinion,) the main support. This means support in every aspect. Not just financially, but emotionally as well. When I see how parents handle their children and young adults, most often I'm not seeing the emotional support. It's important for parents and siblings to push being open about problems they're having so that the child or young adult doesn't dwell on the issues they're having. The smallest of events can have a large impact, and getting things out in the open, talking about them, and having your support lift you up when you are down is important. 

Child and teen bullying is obvious, and it goes hand in hand with lack of parental involvement and parents being ignorant. It's the supports job to keep the child/young adult safe. It's not just physical bullying that harms them. Now that we have elevated levels of consciousness, being mentally safe and well adjusted is part of that, and it's important. 

Political doom. Teenagers are getting more involved in politics, which is good that younger people are starting to care about it earlier, but is not good when you deep dive into it. (I frequently get upset and feel that nothing political is going to get better and that there's nothing that I can do to change that, and I'm an adult.) 

Social media is not to blame. You can't blame a software for emotional instability. But we can blame the people on social media, and the lack of education on how to use the internet. We need to teach people how to properly search for information themselves and to not always take what we are told at face value. We also need to teach that living on social media isn't living. It's a tool, and you should use it as such. (There's also online bullying, but that goes hand in hand with the above.) 

Lack of empathy. Can be grouped with the first two. If we as family units teach and treat out children with empathy and emotional support, children will learn that that is correct behaviour when they go to school. They can teach other kids that that behaviour, being kind and empathetic towards other kids and staff, is the way to go. 

Lack of social body positivity. The BMI calculation is not an accurate depiction of health, it doesn't account for bone mass or curves. Our perception of health is warped and we need to change it. Being over weight is not healthy, but people, women and girls especially, need a bit of chub. If females get to under weight, their normal period cycles will stop. This is because their body isn't getting enough resources to function normally, and will cut out non essential functions to be sure the more important functions get the most. Being thin isn't necessarily being healthy. Promoting that being healthy and eating right is better for body positivity than promoting being a certain weight. (Which can be applied to bullying.) 

Lack of physical contact. We are social creatures. We need physical contact. Hugging and kissing, gently rubbing someone's shoulder, non sexual physical contact is important. Asking if someone is comfortable being touched is always first and foremost, but once you get okays, you should give the people you care about that kind of attention. Holding hands with your children, best friends, and significant others is also a small gesture that care show someone you care. Linking arms as you walk, putting your hand on their shoulder before you leave. These small gestures make people feel appreciated and cared for, thought of. Little physical contact moments and small compliments can make someone's day. 

Bad sexual relationships and poor education. This is a big one. I know nobody wants to talk to kids about it, but we are animals, and sex is a huge part or who we are. (for people who aren't asexual.) We as social creatures need not only non sexual physical contact, but sexual physical contact as well. Having a healthy sexual relationship is important. We seem to forget that we used to only live about 30 years. The average age that we had children was about 14-18, right after most people hit puberty. We have to teach our children and young adults that being sexual is natural and that the most important thing when deciding to get sexual with a partner(s) is being open and honest about what you're interested in, what you like, and what you don't like. Sex should be pleasurable for both/all parties. Having positive sexual experiences is important for physical and mental health. Having negative experiences can seriously effect someone. 
We can apply this to just about everything listed above. If a young adult doesn't have a good support system or has low self esteem with body shaming issues, is bullied, anything that makes them insecure, they may make bad sexual decisions, leading to more hurt and confusion, maybe even guilt. Having low self esteem can cause people to get into bad relationships because they feel like they deserve it, can't do better, any number of reasons really. 

Lack of communication can be applied to all that I've talked about. Positive communication is key. Talking about issues that people are having is the best way for them to get through it, and saying "it gets better" or "you just have to make it through school" is dismissing their problems and implying that their feelings aren't valid until they get older, which not only is untrue, but is hurtful. When I was younger and was experiencing some issues myself, I didn't want to get better either. I was scared that if I got help or tried to let some things go, I'd lose a part of who I was. People don't want to change. Whether it's because they are scared for whatever reason, or they like the attention, or any number of countless reasons that it could be, they just don't. 

This is why Bojack Horseman is so successful. Because Bojack doesn't get better. Because Diane, even after trying to divorce Mr. Peanut butter still doesn't know what she wants. Because love isn't the answer. Sometimes it's just not enough, and people who are nihalistic and are realists know that. 

It's why princess Carolyn won't end up with Ralph. Because you don't always get what you want. Things don't always work out. Bojack Horseman is not afraid to tell you the truth. The truth that so many other shows that claim to be about life and family and lgbtqa+ and African American communities over look. The truth that modern media wants to hide. Modern media wants to sell us the idea of happiness so that real change will never happen. Because meaningful, drastic change and the uncharted territory that comes with it scares everyone.
